steps.content: [Bright Hospital Bed - Syndicate; Use the Eastside daytime one if it doesn't look comfortable enough]
Sunlight streams through the windows, illuminating a spotless room. A stark contrast to the filth that haunts his nightmares.
For a moment, he believes he's still dreaming, or that death has claimed him once more.
Then he turns. ${PlayerName} is right there, sitting beside the bed. The instant their eyes meet, the expression on that face hardens into undisguised anger.
Only then does the memory rush back... So he brought him back.
steps.female_content: Only then does the memory rush back... So she brought him back.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...As expected. You found me again, Chief, and so quickly. A promise made, a promise kept. I'm impressed.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You've been out for a week. I was starting to wonder if you'd wake up at all.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Are you angry? Ah... now I remember.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: My apologies. I seem to have mistaken you for someone else and acted... rather uncouthly. I hope I didn't hurt you?
You glare at him.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm not the one wrapped up like a mummy in a hospital bed, after all.
You glare at him.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: An "agent" who can't be left alone for five minutes without getting himself killed? I'd be surprised if you could so much as scratch me.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Haha... Don't worry. Thanks to Mania, this body heals rather quickly. I'll be back on my feet in no time. Please, don't mind it.
To hell with that. You do mind it—a lot.

options: Heals quickly, so that gives you license to throw your life away?

choices.text: Heals quickly, so that gives you license to throw your life away?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The way you fight out there isn't how a disciplined agent operates. Do you have a death wish?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...But death doesn't mean much to me. Sooner or later, the Black Rings will bring me back.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Besides... I did tell you. The disciplined agent you remember died two years ago. The "Rust" you see now... different body, different person. Perhaps a little more unhinged. Sorry to disappoint.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Maybe next time I come back, I could choose a form you'd prefer?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Whatever you like. I could return as a woman, if that suits you better.
[1 second of empty scene] Add a shattering glass sound effect to indicate the Chief's composure is breaking.

options: ...Does death really mean nothing to you?

choices.text: ...Does death really mean nothing to you?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Well, it's happened more than once, and I've tried a few ways. I'm quite used to it by now. Maybe next time, you can let me fully experience what it's like to be... erased by the shackles.

A memory stirs within his body. It's the phantom echo of the shackles that had pierced him not long ago. He had felt it all with perfect, excruciating clarity: through his chest, between his ribs, the impossible nearness to his beating heart... a most peculiar, intimate violation.
While those shackles leave other Sinners unharmed, they ravage a body like his. And yet, the pain had left behind a craving for more.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Quite a remarkable power, really. If you wanted, you could tear me apart without much effort. In theory, you could even keep my consciousness from returning to the Black Rings. After all, the shackles have quite the appetite, even greater than the Rings...

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...Heh. That might even count as a release. Not the worst way to go, honestly...
His words hang in the air, met only by a heavy, rigid silence. You let the quiet stretch for a long, deliberate moment before finally speaking.

options: ...I've said it before. Don't talk like that.

choices.text: ...I've said it before. Don't talk like that.

steps.content: ${PlayerName} is furious. Rust doesn't need to guess; the air itself is thick with it. Since his body hasn't died, the memories from not long ago are still perfectly clear.
[Enter Flashback: The Battlefield at the End of Phase 3]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What nonsense is that?! Don't you have things you must do? Weren't you the one who threw away your past just to keep moving forward? Weren't you supposed to be stubborn as hell?!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then stop talking about dying! Open your damn eyes! You've cheated death over and over. This time is no different! No matter how much it hurts, you keep living! Even if it's just out of pure spite! You still have debts to pay, so get up!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Don't you dare use my hands to find your way out. I won't kill you. If you're going to drag me into this, then here's my answer—

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: LIVE! YOU ARE NOT ALLOWED TO DIE!!
[Exit Flashback]
Silhouetted against the dying sun, your face is lost in shadow. But the shackles within him sing with your fury, a clear and violent signal.
And in that moment, he finally understands the terrible weight of his words.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...Sorry. That was a poor joke.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: I won't say it again.

Is it the bandages and the hospital bed, the undeniable image of frailty? His trademark composure, usually so effortless and infuriating, is completely stripped away. For the first time, he looks capable of genuine reflection.
...Or perhaps it's no act. His eyes are open but unfocused, seeing nothing in this room. This raw, unguarded emptiness feels less like an act and more like the truth of him.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...I've been unfair to you. I always believed I was resolute in my purpose, but now I see... secretly seeking death only proves there's a part of me I never acknowledged. A rather pathetic part.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: But you have my word: even if I don't exactly cherish my life, I'm not so eager to accept death, either.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: After all, dying just means my consciousness returns to those nauseating Black Rings. One moment of carelessness, and I'd be dissolved, absorbed... devoured. The thought alone is unbearable. I'd fight with everything I have to escape alive. I'd crawl out if I had to.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Perhaps that's the only thing that's kept me going this long.
He doesn't look at you. His focus retreats to the bandages swathing his hands. The unnatural, ashen grey of his skin persists, and the wounds visible beneath the gauze are stark and bloodless.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...I lost any real sense of being alive a long time ago. I've lasted this long only because of the Black Rings' <color=#fb9259>curse</color>. So... I have only one purpose left.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: To repel the Black Rings and to stop the fanatics spreading them, whatever it takes. For that end, I'm willing to be your ally. I will support you. And I will protect you... because you matter.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: But I can't promise you—nor can I pretend—that I'll cherish my life. The path I've chosen is dangerous. I could die at any moment, become trapped in a Black Ring, and have to claw my way back for who knows how long.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...And by the time I'm back, a person's entire lifetime may have already passed.
Another long silence settles. At last, his gaze shifts, finding you once more.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Chief, use your shackles on me. Your power seems able to glimpse memories even I can't see clearly. So do it now; see as much as you can while you have the chance.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: In my case, the concept of "life" is quite unpredictable. If I can leave you with something of value, that alone would be worth celebrating.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Don't talk like that. Don't act like your life means nothing.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're not alive just for some great "cause." And your life is not just about you alone...

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Sorry to disappoint. But some people are just that stubborn.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: After all... it's the only thing they can hold onto.

He stops you with a smile, offering his hand. The meaning is plain: use the shackles on him. It is indeed the most efficient way. No surveillance needed, no lies to untangle, no suspicion to hold. Besides...
It seems he can still find the dark memories—the ones he fled, the ones he buried. He offers them to you, trusting you to use them well. But...

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Why not? Isn't this exactly what you need most?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What I need, I'll find on my own. Besides, I've had people test it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The shackles can't peer into someone's soul. They've never shown me what I want to see. That time I saw those memories... that was actually you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: People like you, with ties to the Black Rings... It seems you can channel your thoughts through Mania in reverse, feeding them into the shackles. Into me. After realizing that, I can't help but wonder one thing...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Why was it that the memories strong enough to reach me weren't about duty, or the mission, or the path, or the Black Rings—all the things you're always going on about—but the past you keep saying you've let go of?
Seeing the look on his face, you can't help but laugh out loud.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You didn't even realize it yourself, Mr. Agent? Haha. If you care that much about the people you left behind, stop pretending you don't.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...There you go again. Once you've made up your mind about something, you can be rather unreasonable.

options: I don't need to be reasonable.

choices.text: I don't need to be reasonable.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Call it a hope, then. Mine, and others'. That you'd value these bonds as much as we do.
You place the torn letter of will in front of him—a farewell that Thorn refused to accept.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I didn't tell him anything. The 9th Agency followed confidentiality protocols, too.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But after what happened at the Rust, I think he's pieced it together.
[Enter Flashback]

steps.speaker: Thorn
steps.content: ...I know he's not an enemy. I just...
[Exit Flashback]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Thorn asked me to tell you: "The living don't write farewells. If you have something to say, say it to my face."

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And the shop owner, Samuel... and everything else you've tried to leave with me? I'm not accepting any of it. I'm not the one who owes them, the one they want to see. You're still here, so go take care of it yourself.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Say what you need to say to them yourself. Whether you're in a different body, whether you stay silent or out of sight... you might find fewer people care about those things than you think.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Maybe... there are more people out there who don't care where you came from or what you've become. They just want to know how you're doing now.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It doesn't matter how many faces, voices, bodies, or memories you've worn. These past years—every time you threw yourself into the fray—it left a mark. You changed things. And people remember.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: After all that... do you still think being alive isn't real? That death is something you can just treat lightly?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...I see.
He remains silent, head bowed, as if physically weighed down by his thoughts. Time stretches before he finally answers, his voice soft.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...I don't have an answer. Not yet. Maybe... we can talk about it next time?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Every time you say that, you vanish at the first chance. Is that the plan again?
He smiles awkwardly.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Heh, no, not this time. I really do want to think it over. After all... I've never looked at it this way before.
He tilts his head back, gaze fixed on the ceiling as he searches for something true.

But then, the world intrudes: the warmth of sunlight, the faint aroma of bedside flowers, the softness of the blanket, the rhythmic drip of an IV, the sterile bite of disinfectant, even the deep, long-forgotten ache in his bones. These sensations—so vivid, so mundane—rush in like a tide, washing away his still-forming thoughts.

The "spy"—who has been wound tighter than a spring for lifetimes—finally lets his guard down. A deep, bone-weary exhaustion claims him. He wants to keep talking to ${PlayerName}, but a warm, reassuring drowsiness pulls him under completely.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...Give me some time, Chief. This question... it might actually matter.

Outside the door, a nurse catches your eye and gestures you over. Schorl appears in the doorway. If it's here, it's either that they've set their eyes on Rust, or there's a big job for you. Given the timing, it's likely something has flared up in Fraser again. Either way, your time here is up.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The staff will look after you. Get well soon; there are people waiting for answers. And don't think about running away. MBCC has the room secured, and the bed's fitted with restraints. I'm not making the same mistake twice. You—
The words die on your lips. His breathing has deepened, eyes shuttered, his expression softened by an unfamiliar, unguarded smile.
With a soft sigh, you gently pull the blanket to his shoulders and let yourself out, the door clicking shut behind you without a sound.
[Hospital Ward, Night]
Rust is telling the truth. That night, escape is the furthest thing from his mind. He surrenders to sleep, and it takes him deeply.
In that depth, the inescapable shadow of the Black Rings is finally absent. In its place come older dreams... memories worn smooth by time.
[Flashback]

steps.speaker: Underground Elder
steps.content: Brat... you understand me? Quit... quit your crying. You're already lucky. The Black Ring didn't take you... and lucky again, that I found you.

steps.speaker: Underground Elder
steps.content: Come here. Dry your face. You'll eat what I eat. I brought you here... I won't let you die.
[Flashback Scene Change]

steps.speaker: Underground Elder
steps.content: You want a name? Then I'll go ask the priest—
<i><color=#7683a2>No. You give me one.</color><i>
<i><color=#7683a2>You took my old name. You owe me a new one.</color><i>

steps.speaker: Underground Elder
steps.content: ...What a pain. You're not some Overground swine. What do you need a name for...

steps.speaker: Underground Elder
steps.content: ...Alright. I'll call you ■■■. Was my kid's name. Take it.
[Memories Overlap]

steps.speaker: Mine Guard
steps.content: That name of yours is a mouthful, little Outlander. Can't have everyone stumbling over it every time.

steps.speaker: Mine Guard
steps.content: How about a nickname? Makes things easier. Neighbors will remember it.

steps.speaker: Mine Guard
steps.content: You'll be here a long time. Think of it as a new start. How's ■■ sound? Or pick one yourself.
[Memories Overlap]

steps.speaker: Thorn
steps.content: ■■■■?! Thank god you're back! It's ■■. You remember me?

steps.speaker: Thorn
steps.content: ...Right. Codenames now. I'm "Thorn." Got it? And you're "Rust." We both work for the 9th Agency. Partners.

steps.speaker: Thorn
steps.content: "Rust"... does the name ring any bells? That's what everyone calls you.
[Scene Change]

steps.speaker: Shop Owner
steps.content: ...Honestly, just knowing he's alright is enough. He was a regular, you know? My old boss thought about him for two whole years, came up with new dishes he never got to try. If you see him... tell him to visit. I can at least try to cook a few of the old ones.
[Scene Change]

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: If you hear anything about him, good or bad, let us know.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: He'll always be a friend of Rustfire.
[Chief's portrait]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I want to know your real name.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: No matter where you go, how many times you die, what body you use, or what your mission is... you are my friend.
[Back to Reality]
On this rare night free from nightmares, he wakes long before dawn. For a timeless stretch, he simply stares at the ceiling, his thoughts unmoored and drifting.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...This won't do.

His hand comes up, pressing against the fissures marring his body... Good. He hasn't slipped too far. He can still hear it—the distant call of the Black Rings, the susurrus of voices whispering from beyond the chaos.
A sound he hasn't heard in a long time. If only it had come earlier... the shackles might have heard it, too. A cruel twist of fate.
<i><color=#7683a2>...Right on schedule.</color><i>

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Heh... Time to get moving.

Rust pushes himself up and retrieves a small, concealed device. Only a select few official hospitals can handle a case like his. He had scouted each one long in advance, preparing for exactly this moment.
Well, well. Right on cue, here comes his informant.
[Scene Change] Outside MBCC Gate
Hey there, handsome. Wanna settle your tab before skipping town?

He turns. The assassin in white is already there, leaning against the doorframe. No one saw her approach. With her preternatural speed, she slipped past every surveillance system once again, proving it a hollow joke just like the 9th Agency's house arrest.

steps.speaker: Bai Yi
steps.content: Bailing you out last week wasn't cheap. Doubling my fee this time sounds perfectly reasonable, don't you think? Need my help again?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: By all means. The 9th Agency is covering it. Name your price.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Your only concern should be whether you'll live long enough to spend it.

steps.speaker: Bai Yi
steps.content: No sweat. I'm quick on my feet. Even if that woman shows up, she won't catch me. But you...

steps.speaker: Bai Yi
steps.content: Didn't you say you'd wait for them and never run? What's with the sudden change of heart?
Rust pauses, then smiles.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: I'd never run from the Undergrounders. But now... there's someone far more intimidating.
If he stays any longer, leaving may become unthinkable, in every sense of the word. But... that must wait. For now.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Call it a tactical retreat. I did leave him a note, after all.
steps.female_content: Call it a tactical retreat. I did leave her a note, after all.

steps.content: [MBCC Office]

Your drawer is open, the cameras are blind. That man used his last "escape" to case the place—this time, getting back in was effortless. Five Hypercubes are missing from the count. And he even had the nerve to leave a message on your desk.

<i>Dear Chief,

A job came up on short notice that requires some traveling. Forgive me for not saying goodbye in person. My remaining time here must go toward settling other personal debts. And if I delay any longer... well, leaving might become difficult in more ways than one.
So, my apologies. Please don't exhaust yourself using the shackles to track me down. I've copied the MBCC's contact information. Once I arrive, I'll be in touch.

I've also borrowed a small sum for the trip. I promise to repay it with interest—along with that answer I still owe you.

Rust<i>
You crush the note in your fist, then fling it to the corner.

—He guessed you would react this way. Rust smiles, the expression tinged with reluctance, as he turns from you and the fragile sense of life he'd briefly held. He steps into the DisSea Black Ring, letting its depths absorb him, returning to the inescapable road he must walk alone.
But the promise he leaves behind... this time, he means it.
<i>No matter the body I wear, the deaths I endure, or the years that slip by... I will repay every debt I owe you.<i>
